subject: physics

verification.note: Unit 2 has NO Short Answer or Long Answer section in EITHER source book — the Fastrack (pp.4-5) and the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (pp.2-3) both list Very Short Answer questions only. So every Unit 2 card is a 2-mark VSAQ and no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Dimensional analysis is the method in which
a physical quantity is written as powers of
steps.why: Every mechanical quantity is some combination of M, L and T, so writing those powers gives a fingerprint that does not depend on which units are used.
common_mistakes: Saying dimensional analysis gives the numerical value. It gives the powers only, never the constant.

recall.must_convey: That dimensional analysis writes a physical quantity as powers of the fundamental quantities.

steps.memory_tip: Dimensions are the M, L, T fingerprint of a quantity — never the number in front.
steps.margin_note: Say "powers of the fundamental quantities". That phrasing earns the mark.

steps.label: An example
steps.why: Showing where the powers come from — mass times acceleration — proves the method rather than quoting a remembered result.
common_mistakes: Writing [M L T⁻¹], which is momentum, not force.

recall.must_convey: That force has dimensions M L T to the minus two.
accept: mass length time to the minus two

steps.memory_tip: Force = mass × acceleration, so [M][L T⁻²] = [M L T⁻²].
steps.margin_note: Derive it in one line rather than quoting it.

insider_note: Both books ask this. Give the definition and one worked example — the example is the second mark.
